data.title: Nothing to Declare: Steering a single neuron increases concealment in AI teams
data.description: arXiv:2611.24475v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Recent research suggests that individual neurons can have interpretable roles in AI behaviour. In Qwen3.5-4B, steering along one neuron's output direction increased decisions to conceal information more in teams than alone across five scenarios, even when teammates provided no messages. When all members participated and received steering, collective concealment increased in four scenarios, while inter-agent messaging helped temper concealment under steering. Moreover, removing the neuron's contribution had negligible effects. Collective settings can therefore change how an internal intervention affects AI behaviour.
data.author: Edoardo Chidichimo, Felix P. S. Wallis
